html:
A summer festival of music, dance and theatre held among the Roman temples of Baalbek in Lebanon's Beqaa Valley since the mid-1950s.

It was founded with the backing of President Camille Chamoun, when Beirut was a cosmopolitan city of banks and tourism. The stages stand beside the temples of Jupiter and Bacchus, among the best preserved Roman ruins anywhere. Orchestras, ballet and theatre companies and jazz musicians came from Europe and America.

The festival also launched Lebanese art. From 1957 the Rahbani brothers and Fairuz staged their "Lebanese Nights" there, musical plays built on village life and folk dance. They helped shape a Lebanese national culture.

The civil war stopped the festival in 1975, and the Beqaa became a base for armed groups. It came back in 1997 and has gone on since, though wars and crises have cancelled or moved some seasons.
sum: A summer festival of music, dance and theatre held among the Roman temples of Baalbek in Lebanon's Beqaa Valley since the mid-1950s.
